# Risk-Focused Requirements Checklist: Slideshow Background Music Playback

**Purpose**: Author pre-planning review of requirements quality in the feature's
highest-risk areas — skin-file integration, BGM lifecycle/fade timing, source
configuration, and error/notification handling — before running `/speckit-plan`
downstream artifacts are trusted.
**Created**: 2026-09-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Skin Integration Safety (FR-015, Edge Case 5)

- [ ] CHK001 Is the precise set of installation failure modes (not found / not readable / not writable / parse failure) enumerated in spec.md itself, matching what contracts/skin-integration.md details, or does spec.md only assert failure "for instance because the skin's files are not writable" without the full set? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK002 Does spec.md define what "preserve a copy of any skin file it modifies" means on a second or later install attempt, where a backup already exists? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK003 Is "re-establish it after the user changes skins" bound to a specific trigger (e.g., next profile login only) in spec.md, or does the wording leave open whether re-establishment could also happen some other way? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the criteria for recognizing "the integration is already present" (so it is not duplicated) specified precisely enough in spec.md to be independently implemented, or does spec.md defer entirely to design-time detail? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015]
- [x] CHK005 Does spec.md address the case where more than one slideshow-integration target file exists for the active skin (e.g., multiple resolution variants)? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [x] CHK006 Is there a bound on how long the addon may remain silently non-functional after a skin update drops the integration (Edge Case 5), beyond "the next time the user's profile is loaded"? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Case 5]
- [ ] CHK007 Does spec.md state whether the preserved backup copy is ever used to restore the original file (e.g., on addon uninstall), or is that explicitly out of scope? [Gap]

## BGM Lifecycle & Fade Timing (FR-001–003, FR-013, SC-001–003)

- [x] CHK008 Does User Story 1's "music starts playing shortly after the slideshow starts" (Independent Test) use language precise enough to be read as consistent with SC-001's 2-second bound, or could the two be read as different timing expectations? [Consistency, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "no audible overlap" in SC-002 quantified (e.g., a maximum permissible gap or crossfade tolerance), or left to subjective judgment? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK010 Does the spec define expected behavior if a transition cannot complete within its stated budget (e.g., slow storage delays playback start past the 2-second window)? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [x] CHK011 Are resume semantics (FR-003, "the following track") fully specified for a BGM playlist containing exactly one track? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK012 Does the spec define outcome when a video clip ends at the same moment the slideshow itself exits — does FR-003's resume ever begin, or does FR-004's teardown take precedence with no observable resume? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [x] CHK013 Is "normal volume" (SC-001, SC-002) defined as a fixed target, or explicitly tied to the user's existing Kodi volume setting at the time? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK014 Are the FR-013 1-second fade duration and the SC-001/SC-002/SC-003 2-second budgets cross-checked for consistency in all three transition cases, including where the remaining ~1 second of headroom is assumed to go? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013]

## Settings & Source Configuration (FR-005–008, FR-011, FR-014)

- [ ] CHK015 Are validation requirements specified for a file that matches a supported extension (FR-006) but is corrupt or unplayable, beyond "no playable audio" in FR-010? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [x] CHK016 Does the spec require re-validating a directory-based BGM source at slideshow start (paralleling FR-012's playlist-file check), or is directory validity checked only once, at selection time (FR-011)? [Consistency, Gap]
- [ ] CHK017 Is shuffle behavior (FR-008) specified for whether the random order is re-rolled every slideshow start, or fixed once per configuration change? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK018 Does FR-014's "stop any music already playing in Kodi's player" specify scope precisely — music player only, or any active media playback — so it cannot be read either way? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK019 Is SC-004's "next time they start a slideshow" explicit about what happens if a setting is changed while a slideshow is already in progress (deferred vs. rejected mid-session)? [Clarity, Spec §SC-004]

## Error Handling & Notifications (FR-011, FR-012, FR-015)

- [ ] CHK020 Is the underlying rule that decides blocking dialog (FR-011) vs. non-blocking notification (FR-012, FR-015) stated as a general criterion in spec.md, or only demonstrated case-by-case, leaving a reader to infer the rule? [Clarity, Gap]
- [ ] CHK021 Does spec.md define what happens if the FR-011 blocking dialog is left unacknowledged (timeout, default action), or is indefinite waiting the only specified behavior? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK022 Are the non-blocking notifications (FR-012, FR-015) specified with enough detail (e.g., minimum visible duration) to be objectively verified as "notified," or is any transient popup sufficient by the current wording? [Measurability, Gap]
- [x] CHK023 Is the requirement that logged failures carry a "specific reason" and "suggested remedy" (FR-015) stated in spec.md itself, or does spec.md rely on contracts/skin-integration.md for that detail with no cross-reference? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK024 Are FR-011 and FR-012 consistent on whether the user is told which specific source (path/filename) failed, or does one specify that detail while the other does not? [Consistency]

## Cross-Cutting Traceability

- [x] CHK025 Are the two open risks recorded in plan.md as blocking `/speckit-tasks` trust — R-5 (whether a `.pls`/`.xsp` track can be targeted for FR-003's next-track resume) and R-6 (whether the clip-start callback arrives early enough for FR-013's fade-in) — reflected anywhere in spec.md's Assumptions, or does spec.md read as if FR-003 and FR-013 are already fully settled? [Traceability, Gap]
- [x] CHK026 If R-5 or R-6 resolve unfavorably, does spec.md indicate which requirement text would need to change, or would that surface only in plan.md/research.md? [Gap, Assumption]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`

### Review log — 2026-09-12

Re-reviewed against spec.md as amended (FR-016, Assumption 8) and the downstream
research.md/data-model.md/contracts changes (D-012, D-013). Eight items were satisfied
already; a follow-up pass fixed five more directly in spec.md. Thirteen remain open.

**Checked in the first pass, with rationale**:

- **CHK006** — "next profile login" is the tightest bound achievable without a
  persistent service (forbidden by constitution 2.2); the spec already states it as the
  bound, and no finer-grained one is achievable given the architecture.
- **CHK012** — FR-004 already settles the race: "background music MUST NOT resume after
  the slideshow has exited" applies regardless of what FR-003 would otherwise do,
  independent of exact callback ordering.
- **CHK013** — FR-016 (added this session) ties the fade-in target and restore level to
  "the most recently observed volume while background music was last audible" — i.e.,
  "normal volume" is the user's own current setting, not a fixed value.
- **CHK014** — the 2026-09-11 Clarifications entry explicitly reasons through the
  1s-fade-within-2s-budget math for all three SCs; SC-001 and SC-003 state what their
  window covers.
- **CHK018** — FR-014 and User Story 3 Scenario 5 both scope the setting to "music
  already playing," not general media playback.
- **CHK023** — FR-015 already states "MUST log the specific reason together with a
  suggested remedy" directly in spec.md text, not only in contracts/skin-integration.md.
- **CHK025, CHK026** — closed by this session's Assumption 8, which names R-5/R-6
  explicitly and states which requirement clause changes if either resolves unfavorably.

**Checked in the second pass — spec.md fixed directly**:

- **CHK005** — FR-015 now states every resolution-variant file must be integrated, none
  left out, matching what contracts/skin-integration.md already specified.
- **CHK008** — User Story 1's Independent Test now cites SC-001's 2-second bound instead
  of "shortly after."
- **CHK011** — FR-003 now states a single-track BGM playlist resumes into itself,
  consistent with Assumption 5's loop-back behavior.
- **CHK016** — FR-012 and Edge Case 2 now cover a directory BGM source becoming invalid
  at slideshow start, not only a playlist file — matching what data-model.md's
  validation table already assumed (`FR-012` applied to `path` regardless of `kind`).
- **CHK019** — SC-004 now states a mid-slideshow setting change does not affect the
  session already in progress.

**Still open (13 items)**: CHK001–004, CHK007, CHK009, CHK010, CHK015, CHK017,
CHK020–022, CHK024. None of these were touched — they're the lower-priority items from
the fix/defer triage: skin-integration detail that already lives in
contracts/skin-integration.md (CHK001–004, CHK007), genuine but low-probability edge
cases (CHK009, CHK010, CHK015, CHK017), and the notification rule's lack of a stated
general principle plus minor measurability/symmetry gaps (CHK020–022, CHK024). Accepted
as deferred, documented risk rather than fixed, per the 2026-09-12 triage discussion.
